Run an LLM Locally on Mac With Ollama

On an Apple Silicon Mac, open Ollama and download the small qwen2.5:0.5b model. Send a test prompt to 127.0.0.1:11434, then run ollama ps to see which model actually loaded. You need internet access for the app and model downloads. The test uses plain text.

  1. Install Ollama and download the model
  2. Send a prompt and verify the loaded model
  3. Find the next step if it fails
  4. Test results and source files

Install Ollama and download a small model

  1. Get Ollama for macOS and open it. Its download page lists the supported macOS versions. If the setup offers to install the command-line tool, complete that step before opening Terminal.
  2. Check the running service and download the exact tag below. The model listing showed a 398 MB download when checked November 28, 2026. Allow extra disk space for Ollama and temporary download files.
ollama --version
ollama pull qwen2.5:0.5b
ollama list

The last command should show qwen2.5:0.5b. For an interactive chat, run ollama run qwen2.5:0.5b; type /bye to exit. Keep the exact local tag when trying the API. Ollama also lists cloud models, which run on its servers.

Send a prompt and verify the loaded model

Use the synthetic prompt below. With the standard local Ollama service running, the response is a JSON object with an assistant message. Check for done: true, then immediately inspect ollama ps.

curl --noproxy '*' --fail-with-body -sS \
  http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/chat \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary '{
    "model": "qwen2.5:0.5b",
    "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly LOCAL_OK and nothing else."}],
    "options": {"num_ctx":2048,"temperature":0,"num_predict":16},
    "stream": false,
    "keep_alive": "60s"
  }'
ollama ps

Look for the requested tag in ollama ps. Its processor column describes where Ollama loaded the model. Compare CPU, GPU and split readings if the placement is unexpected. Control how long this model stays loaded. A different reply can still confirm execution if the request completed and the model appears in the running list. To free memory after the test, run ollama stop qwen2.5:0.5b once no other work needs that model. The model stays downloaded. To remove downloaded files, delete the exact Ollama tag and check disk use.

For a stronger local-only check, finish downloading first, then repeat the request with your Mac disconnected from its external networks if doing so will not interrupt other work. Keep the request pointed at loopback, the address that refers to this Mac. This checks whether that request works without an internet connection.

What happened on the first request?

See stepsSee stepsSee steps

Connection refused or Ollama unavailable

Open the Ollama app and try curl --noproxy '*' -fsS http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/version. A response containing a version confirms the service answered. If you started Ollama on a different port, use that same port for the API and the CLI. Leave the service bound to loopback for this test.

Ollama says the model is missing

Run ollama list and check the complete tag. If it is absent, run ollama pull qwen2.5:0.5b while connected and wait for the download to finish. Check free storage if the download fails. Try the same request again once the tag appears.

Import an official GGUF if the registry download fails

Download the Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M GGUF from Qwen. Work in the folder with the downloaded file. Save the line below as Modelfile alongside it, then import under a new tag. If a model already uses the example name, pick a fresh name.

FROM ./qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf
ollama create qwen-local-first -f Modelfile
ollama list

See how Ollama resolves paths in a Modelfile. Once qwen-local-first:latest appears, replace qwen2.5:0.5b with qwen-local-first in the test request and the stop command. The registry tag and the separately published GGUF can differ. Keep extra free disk space for Ollama’s imported copy.

A reply appeared, or the result is unclear

Look for an error message in the JSON and check the running list immediately. If the model unloaded before you checked, repeat the request and run ollama ps within the keep-alive period. If Ollama reports insufficient memory, close unused workloads or test a smaller model with a short context. Verify the running context value before assuming a setting took effect.

If you chose LM Studio instead, check its local server and model ID.

Test results and source files

On November 28, 2026, an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 26.4.1 and Ollama 0.40.18 started with an empty model directory. The registry pull failed when Ollama rejected the storage redirect in this network environment. The Qwen GGUF import succeeded on a separate test port, 11440. The assistant replied LOCAL_OK, ollama ps showed the imported tag at 2,048 context tokens with 100% GPU, and the running-model list was empty after it was stopped.

We restarted the test process with the model already on disk and a loopback-only network policy. The same request succeeded. A separate process under the same policy could not open an external connection. The Mac itself stayed connected, and the test used a command-line build of Ollama. Download the request, replies and running-model snapshots.

For comparison, an earlier run with an imported Qwen GGUF reported approximately 297 MiB at a 2,048-token context and 419 MiB at 8,192 using Ollama’s running-model size field. The same model file was used for both requests in that earlier run. These are runtime-reported model sizes for that fixture. Free memory, peak usage and the suitability of larger models were outside that check.

Sources checked November 28, 2026: Ollama quickstart, Qwen model tag, running-model API and processor column and local settings. For a client that uses the OpenAI SDK, connect to the local /v1 API and diagnose 404s. For a step-by-step overview, see the Ollama setup and endpoint checks. For an editor or coding CLI, connect OpenCode to the same local Ollama server. For a second runtime, see the Ollama and LM Studio same-file test.
